input.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet HSE gap for Cu2O (mp-361) is 1.56 eV, below the 2.06 eV photon energy, so Cu-rich oxides should absorb at 602 nm. BiVO4 (~2.4 eV) would not. Candidate 74 has Cu/V near 3:2 (a Cu3V2O8-type vanadate with a gap of about 1.8–2 eV), so it is a sensible first probe of the Cu-vanadate photoanode region. I could not get IDs for the ternary phases, so this is indirect evidence.

content.text:
I submitted **index 74** (Bi 0.07 / Cu 0.54 / V 0.39). It gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, 1.7e-7 A under 2.06 eV (602 nm) light. With only three measurements, I can't tell how close that is to the best composition in the library.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 74 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 | **1.7e-7 A** |
| 73 | 0.09 / 0.48 / 0.44 | 1.2e-7 A |
| 108 | 0.28 / 0.54 / 0.18 | 0 A |

**How I chose them:**
- **Index 74:** its Cu:V ratio is close to a copper vanadate (Cu₃V₂O₈-type), and those typically have band gaps small enough to absorb 602 nm light.
- **Index 108:** this was a test of a different region, a Cu-rich, low-V composition near BiCu₂VO₆. It gave nothing, probably because CuO or CuBi₂O₄ forms there.
- **Index 73:** a neighbour of 74 with Cu:V nearer 1:1, which the Gaussian-process suggester (`gp_suggest`) also ranked highest. It came out lower than 74.

**Limitations:**
- **Weak model evidence:** the list of known phases was too large to return, so I never got IDs for the three-cation phases. The required model checks behind each measurement therefore used only band gaps of simple oxides: Cu₂O 1.56 eV, V₂O₅ 2.83 eV, CuO 0.32 eV.
- **XRD not used:** none of the 5 XRD measurements were spent, so I have no confirmation of which crystal phases are present.
- **Unexplored regions:** I didn't measure the Bi-richer part of the V-rich compositions (e.g. index 6 or 60). I also didn't try index 75, which has more Cu than 73 but still less than 74.
